memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "From there he went up to Beersheba. That night the LORD appeared to him and said, 'I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you; I will bless you and will increase the number of your descendants for the sake of my servant Abraham.' Isaac built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD. There he pitched his tent, and there his servants dug a well." - Gen 26:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After all the conflict over the wells, Isaac arrives in Beersheba, and that very night God appears to him with words of tender reassurance: "Do not be afraid, for I am with you." What a gift after a stressful season. God meets Isaac not with a rebuke but with comfort and the promise of His presence.

"Do not be afraid, for I am with you" — these are among the sweetest words in all of Scripture, spoken again and again to God's people. Notice the reason we need not fear: not that our problems vanish, but that God is with us. His presence is the answer to our fears.

Look at Isaac's response. He does not just receive the promise; he builds an altar and calls on the name of the Lord. He worships. When God draws near, the fitting response is to make room for Him at the centre of our lives.

Whatever season you are in, hear God's word to Isaac as an echo of His heart toward you in Christ, who promised, "I am with you always" (Matt 28:20). You need not be afraid, because you are not alone. Build your "altar" — make worship and prayer the settled centre of your life — and let His presence steady your heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What fear do I need to surrender to the God who is with me?
2. Is worship the settled centre of my life, as it was for Isaac?
3. How does Jesus' promise "I am with you always" comfort me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for Your promise, "Do not be afraid, for I am with you." Steady my fearful heart with Your presence, and make worship the centre of my life. Amen.
